Pancreatitis is one of the major complications of endoscopic retrograde cholangio-pancreatography (ERCP) and endoscopic sphincterotomy (ES).
It is continues to be associated with substantial morbidity and occasional mortality.

Although post-ERCP pancreatitis often has been viewed as an unpredictable and unavoidable, there have been ongoing attempts to minimize the incidence and severity of post-ERCP pancreatitis by identifying high-risk patients in whom other methods of diagnosis and treatment should be considered first, by developing endoscopic interventions that can limit ERCP-induced pancreatic injury, and by identifying pharmacological agents that could be administered before or during the procedure.
Recent study showed phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE-5) inhibitors which act at the level of intracellular signal transmission to relax smooth muscles.
This relaxation effect on smooth muscle is due to intracellular accumulation of cGMP, secondary to inhibition of the PDE responsible for degradation of this intracellular messenger.
We found that vardenafil affected basal pressure and amplitude in the SO.
The decreases in basal pressure and amplitude in patients with suspected SOD after administration of vardenafil were statistically significant.
In addition, the decreases in basal pressure and amplitude after administration of vardenafil were statistically significant regardless of SOD type.
Administration of PDE-5 inhibitors prior to ERCP to decrease SO tone may reduce the incidence of post-ERCP pancreatitis.

Prospective placebo-controlled clinical trials are required to determine whether PDE-5 inhibitors are effective in the treatment of SOD and prevention of post-ERCP pancreatitis.Pancreatitis is one of the major complications of endoscopic retrograde cholangio-pancreatography (ERCP) and endoscopic sphincterotomy (ES).
